Chip stocks dump again Summary: RBA Governor Bullock said inflation risks remain skewed to the upside, and the minutes showed six of nine members judged 4.85% “not clearly sufficient”. Three warned of a sharper downturn. New Zealand one-year inflation expectations jumped to 2.92%, while the two-year gauge held near 2.36%. Respondents see the OCR at 3.05% by year-end. Former BOJ chief Kuroda said rates may need to rise above neutral. Japan postponed its planned two-year floating-rate bond. Brent eased to around $91.80 on surplus expectations despite a tanker attack near Hormuz and Iranian claims of four strikes. Gold steadied near $3,868 after Monday’s one-year low. The Nikkei fell about 0.9%, the Kospi about 1.8% and Samsung more than 3% after the US imposed chip export licensing on five countries. The Reserve Bank of Australia set the tone in Asia on Tuesday. Governor Michele Bullock said inflation risks remain skewed to the upside, and minutes of the November meeting showed most board members judged the 4.85% cash rate “not clearly sufficient” to bring inflation back to target. Regional stocks fell as US chip export curbs weighed on technology names. Oil eased on expectations of a supply surplus, despite a fresh tanker attack near the Strait of Hormuz. Levels below are as of around 04:35 GMT. Central banks The RBA minutes revealed a divided board behind November’s hike. Six members cited rising inflation pressures, strong services inflation and a likely higher neutral rate. Three dissenters warned the economy might be nearing a materially sharper downturn. The board gave no explicit guidance. The minutes also noted that the forecasts assume oil prices fall by around US$30 a barrel over two years, leaving significant upside risk if prices stay high. AUD/USD held near 0.6740. In New Zealand, the RBNZ’s Survey of Expectations showed one-year inflation expectations jumping to 2.92% from 2.60%, while the closely watched two-year measure edged up only to 2.36%. Respondents expect the official cash rate to rise to 3.05% by year-end from 2.75%, ahead of the 9 December Monetary Policy Statement. NZD/USD was little changed near 0.5495. In Japan, former BOJ Governor Haruhiko Kuroda said rates may need to rise above neutral if inflation worsens, citing cost pressures from the Iran war. He also called the government’s planned food sales tax cut inflationary. Separately, the Finance Ministry postponed its planned two-year floating-rate government bond, according to sources, because markets already price in BOJ hikes. USD/JPY eased to around 159.20, and the 10-year JGB yield was near 2.89%. Oil and geopolitics Brent slipped to around $91.80 a barrel as an International Energy Agency forecast of a fourth-quarter supply surplus outweighed renewed attacks on shipping. A tanker transiting Hormuz was disabled near Khasab, Oman, according to UK maritime authorities, and Iran’s navy claimed four tanker strikes in 24 hours. The US Army is seeking to build 17 concrete bunkers at bases in Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon. CNN reported US intelligence on Iranian contingency planning for an attack in Washington, which officials said was not imminent. The surplus narrative is driving prices for now, but such explanations tend to follow price and can change quickly. Gold Gold steadied near $3,868 an ounce, up around 0.3%, after touching a one-year low near $3,830 on Monday as Treasury yields above 5% and a firm dollar weighed. Bank views remain sharply divided. Morgan Stanley named gold its top commodity pick, with a $5,250 target for late 2027, while Goldman Sachs sees $4,650. Silver rose about 1%. Equities Asian stocks fell after the US required licenses for advanced chip exports to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil, aiming to curb Chinese access to AI computing: The Nikkei 225 lost about 0.9% to around 59,100, and the Topix fell around 1.7%. The Kospi dropped roughly 1.8%, with Samsung Electronics down more than 3%. The Hang Seng slipped about 0.8%, and the Shanghai Composite was flat. US futures were mixed: S&P 500 futures were little changed and Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.3%. Bitcoin held near $64,950. Bank views Goldman Sachs Asset Management expects Fed hikes in both December and January after a third firm reading on core inflation. PIMCO urged investors to lock in bond yields near 25-year highs. Morgan Stanley set an 8,700 S&P 500 target for end-2027. Goldman Sachs forecast a 24% return for the Topix over the next 12 months, saying Japan’s rally may broaden to more sectors.
